article.title: Palabras variables
article.part: Unidades gramaticales y clases de palabras — Unidades gramaticais e classes de palavras
article.chapter: Clases de palabras — Classes de palavras

claims.summary: Las palabras variables son palabras que pueden cambiar de forma para expresar información gramatical como género, número, persona, tiempo o modo.

En portugués, sustantivos, muchos adjetivos, artículos y numerosos pronombres pueden variar en género o número: 'o livro / os livros', 'a casa bonita / as casas bonitas'. Los verbos presentan otro tipo de variación.
Examples include 'menino → meninos' (singular to plural noun change), 'bonita → bonitas' (adjective concordance with plural noun), and 'falo → falamos' (verb change according to person and number).

links.notes: The article explicitly defines 'palavras variáveis' as words that can change form to express grammatical information, which aligns with the general claim about variable words in Portuguese.

The article provides examples of how nouns, adjectives, articles, and pronouns change in gender and number, as well as how verbs change in person, number, and tense, supporting the general claim about the variability of Portuguese words.
The article provides concrete examples of noun and verb inflection, demonstrating the general claim about the grammatical changes in Portuguese words.
